findings.description: The instance user_data script embeds hardcoded AWS access key ID (AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMAAA) and secret access key (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) in plaintext. These credentials are readable by anyone with describe permissions on the instance and any leaked user data, constituting a credential compromise.

The EBS volume is created without the encrypted flag set to true (the encrypted=false line explicitly commented out), leaving the volume unencrypted at rest. Sensitive data stored on the volume is exposed to anyone who gains access to the underlying storage.
This EBS snapshot is created without enabling encryption, so it inherits the unencrypted state of its source volume. Unencrypted snapshots expose data at rest and, when shared, can leak data.
The security group opens SSH port 22 to 0.0.0.0/0, granting the entire internet access to the instance's SSH service, enabling brute-force or remote login attacks from arbitrary hosts.

The security group opens HTTP port 80 to 0.0.0.0/0. While a web server needs inbound traffic, the guidance/benchmark notes unrestricted ingress grants access to the entire internet; combined with the lack of TLS on the public web port this expands attack surface beyond intended boundaries.
The security group allows all outbound traffic (protocol -1, all ports, to 0.0.0.0/0). Unrestricted egress provides a data exfiltration path and a channel to command-and-control infrastructure.

map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IPv4 addresses to instances launched in the subnet, exposing the instance to the internet instead of placing it in a private subnet without public addressing.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IPv4 addresses to instances launched in this second subnet, exposing resources to the internet.
